description: Reverses wavecycles in groups of cyclecnt: the material inside each group plays backwards while the groups themselves stay in order. Output duration is static and SAMPLE-EXACT (88200/44100 frames preserved on 2 s / 1 s tones, enveloped noise and flat noise at cyclecnt 2-30). At cyclecnt 1 each individual cycle is flipped (legal; subtle phase-mangling); larger groups reverse longer stretches, producing audible micro-retrogrades whose grain size follows the source's pitch. Deterministic. MONO only.
musical_use: Micro-retrograde texturing: the sound keeps its overall envelope and length but its cellular material runs backwards in beads. Small groups (2-8 cycles) give a subtle phasey 'wrongness' to pitched material; bigger groups (30-100+) chop speech and melody into clearly-reversed granules - the classic 'tape-chopped backwards' effect without any editing. A breakpointed cyclecnt morphs from intact to heavily-retrograded across the file. Pairs well before distort envel or reform when you want the reversal grain to survive further waveset mangling.

cyclecnt.description: Number of wavecycles per reversed group (CDP-enforced 1-32767; 0 refused 'Parameter[1] Value (0.000000) out of range (1.000000 to 32767.000000)'). Breakpoint-capable, banner-confirmed ('cyclecnt may vary in time') and verified: a 2->30 ramp differs from both endpoint scalar renders while staying sample-exact in length.

examples.description: Subtle phasey grit: reverse every 4 cycles.
examples.expected_use: Same-length output; pitched sources gain a hollow, comb-like edge while remaining recognisable.
The file starts nearly intact and dissolves into obviously backwards granules.

known_issues: Unipolar / zero-crossing-free material refused: 'ERROR: CANNOT ACHIEVE TASK: / ERROR: source sound too short to attempt this process.' (exit 255).
Stereo refused: 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255) -> mono.
Deterministic: two runs 1.2 s apart decoded-identical.
Duration static and sample-exact in all 8 probe runs (tones, enveloped noise, flat noise, breakpointed cyclecnt).
